items.title: XRISM Sees a Star’s Wind Power Its Companion’s Flares
items.body: NASA reports that astronomers using the Japan-led XRISM observatory directly observed a giant star’s stellar wind being captured by its compact companion, powering strong X-ray flares. The target is BP Crucis, a high-mass X-ray binary about 13,000 light-years away in the southern constellation Crux.

discussion.body: The key marker is “good for”: well-being concerns a person’s own life, rather than goodness in general.
So “Is this morally admirable?” and “Is this good for the person?” are different questions, not synonyms.

items.title: Well-Being Is About What Makes a Life Go Well
items.body: Philosophical well-being asks how well a person’s life is going for that person: which ultimate goods make it worth living from their point of view. It is prudential value, distinct from moral or aesthetic value.

sources.title: Many Jewish faculty and staff say university EDI is failing them

discussion.body: The disconnect is striking: universities have EDI infrastructure built to address discrimination, yet the very group experiencing a surge in hate crimes says those offices went silent when they needed them most.

But the survey also shows Canadian students have low negativity toward Jews personally. The hostility is directed at Israel, not Jewish individuals. EDI offices may be struggling to distinguish political criticism from antisemitism — a genuine policy dilemma, not simple indifference.

Research cited in the piece notes higher education usually increases tolerance. The gap between that expectation and what Jewish faculty are reporting suggests something specific has broken in how these offices handle Israel-related tensions.

items.title: Canadian Jewish faculty say university EDI offices met them with silence after Oct. 7
items.body: A federally commissioned survey and a new study find that Jewish faculty and staff at Canadian universities say equity, diversity and inclusion offices largely failed to engage with their concerns after the Hamas attack. While Jewish students report low personal negativity from peers, they encounter high negativity toward Israel — a friction point because many Canadian Jews feel emotionally attached to Israel and support its existence. In 2025, Jewish people were the target of 70 per cent of all police-reported hate crimes directed at a religious group in Canada, despite making up about one per cent of the population.

discussion.body: Gamma-ray telescopes are rare because gamma rays don't focus like light — they penetrate. COSI's wide-field Compton imaging design lets it watch large swaths of the sky for the brief flashes of antimatter annihilation and supernova nucleosynthesis.

The partnership list is notable: a university lab leading, with NASA Goddard, a defense contractor (Northrop), and the Italian Space Agency all contributing. That's the modern model — distributed expertise across sectors and borders.

items.title: NASA's COSI telescope will hunt gamma rays from antimatter and dying stars
items.body: The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) is coming together at UC Berkeley. This wide-field gamma-ray telescope will study the Milky Way's most energetic phenomena: the creation and destruction of matter and antimatter, and the final stages of stellar lives. The detector assembly — seen in a July 8 image being lifted into place — uses flex circuits covered in silver material to carry signals to readout electronics. It's a collaboration spanning UC Berkeley's Space Sciences Lab, UC San Diego, the Naval Research Laboratory, NASA Goddard, Northrop Grumman, Space Dynamics Laboratory, the Italian Space Agency, and other institutions.

sources.title: FAA tees up $875M AI tool to help manage air traffic congestion

discussion.body: An AI advisor for the world's most congested airspace is a high-stakes test. If SMART cuts delays and near-misses in the D.C. corridor, the case for nationwide deployment gets much stronger.

The system only *advises* controllers — it doesn't issue commands. That human-in-the-loop design is deliberate, but it also means the AI's value depends entirely on whether controllers trust and act on its suggestions in real time.

Mann's endorsement carries weight: he spent 17 years at the FAA in multiple roles and now advises on aviation safety and AI governance. His 'right call' verdict reflects institutional caution, not just vendor optimism.

items.title: FAA to debut AI air-traffic advisor over Washington, D.C. as soon as Monday
items.body: The FAA's SMART system — an AI tool that predicts traffic flows and flags potential conflicts using airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, and airspace conditions — could go live for the three major D.C.-area airports on September 21. It's the first step toward a planned nationwide rollout across the 29 million square miles of U.S. airspace. Aviation safety consultant Philip Mann, a 17-year FAA veteran, called the limited-scope launch the 'right call' before scaling nationally.

sources.title: What Came Before the American Suburb?

discussion.body: The pre-suburb town wasn't a utopia — it was built on colonized land — but its physical form (dense, walkable, mixed-use) is exactly what urban planners now try to recreate through zoning reform.

The irony: we spent 70 years engineering the suburb, and now spend billions trying to undo its worst effects. Hempstead's Main Street in 1910 had a furniture store, a pharmacy, a commercial block at a street intersection — all within walking distance.

items.title: What the American landscape looked like before the suburb took over
items.body: Before the post-WWII explosion of suburbs, highways, and malls, places like Hempstead Village, New York, show what small-town life looked like. Founded in the mid-1600s under Dutch control, the land was purchased in 1643 by two Englishmen, John Carman and John Fordham, who negotiated with local Indigenous tribes. Families moved in the following year to establish a community centered on a Main Street with storefronts, pharmacies, and commercial blocks — a walkable, mixed-use pattern that vanished once mass automobile ownership and federal highway funding reshaped the country.

discussion.body: Managed endpoints allow teams to deploy models without managing infrastructure, letting AWS handle operations as S5E3 describes the console, SDK, and CLI pathways.
HyperPod Inference targets teams requiring Kubernetes-native control over dedicated GPU clusters, addressing the GPU capacity constraints and cold start challenges S5E1 identifies.

items.title: SageMaker AI 2026 Inference Capabilities and Deployment Paths
items.body: Generative AI inference presents unique challenges: models range from tens to hundreds of gigabytes, latency is measured in tokens per second, and cold starts can span multiple minutes as containers and weights transfer, with GPU capacity constrained and traditional monitoring tools lacking token-level signals, as S5E1 describes. Amazon SageMaker AI offers two deployment paths: managed endpoints for teams wanting AWS to handle infrastructure, and HyperPod Inference for teams needing Kubernetes-native control over dedicated GPU clusters, as S5E3 states. Year-to-date in 2026, SageMaker AI has delivered 13 new capabilities across these two paths for enterprises, startups, and the public sector, as S5E6 reports.
